text: Report on Transplanting Rare Plants from the Bad Creek Area In 1973 Joseph Green and I made a botanical survey of the Bad Creek Area of Oconee County, S. C. for Duke Power Company. We discovered five plants which we considered rare, four of which we thought should be protected by transplanting. The five plants were Panax quinquefolium L. (ginseng), Lysimachia fraseri Duby (Fraser's lysimachia), Lygodium palmatum (Bernh.) Swartz (American climbing fern), Gaultheria procumbens L. (wintergreen), and Fothereilla major (Sims) Lodd. (witch-alder). We recommended to the environmentalists of Duke Power Company that all but Lysimachia be transplanted in similar sites nearby. At that time we did not include Lysimachia because of its abundance in areas adjacent to the one studied. Officials of the company asked me to supervise the transplanting. By the middle of July, 1974 we completed the relocation of these plants. Once we began planting, we also included some Lysimachia just to be sure that plenty of the plants will survive in the vicinity. I was assisted by Jim Sevic, John Garton, and Bob Gudger -- all biologists on the Duke staff.
